# SwiftUI enhancement policy

`enhance-execute` owns workflow order and builds. This policy defines the final SwiftUI shape. Treat screenshots and Locofy source values as exact. Preserve existing target behavior unless the file plan explicitly changes it.

## Read first

Use the completed planning artifacts:

- `.locofy/agent/memory/file-plan.md`
- `.locofy/agent/memory/state-variants.md`
- `.locofy/agent/memory/generated-component-groups.md`
- `<incoming>/.locofy/agent/memory/screenshot-mapping.md`

Apply those decisions directly. The bundled probe is the detailed executable specification; do not duplicate it with ad hoc scans.

## Project and feature shape

Bootstrap the final layout before writing screens when the target is still flat:

```text
Features/Booking/
  Views/BookingView.swift
  ViewModels/BookingViewModel.swift
  Models/BookingModel.swift
DesignSystem/
  DesignTokens.swift
  AppFonts.swift
  IconNames.swift
  ColorNames.swift
  AccessibilityCommon.swift
Localization.swift
AppConstants.swift
AccessibilityIdentifiers.swift
RootTabView.swift              # when the design has tabs
UIComponents/BottomNavigation/BottomNavigationView.swift # when the design has tabs
Colors.xcassets/Contents.json
```

- Name screens and private supporting views with a `View` suffix. Every reusable component `struct` and its file use the same `View`-suffixed name. Example: `Button1View` and `ButtonView1` canonicalize to `ButtonView.swift`. Preserve an established target name when reusing an existing component.
- Keep exactly one top-level type declaration in each file under `Models/`. Supporting enums and value types are not exceptions: give each its own model file instead of declaring it beside another model. Every type stored under `Models/` and its file use the same `Model`-suffixed name.
- A screen with mutable state owns an `@MainActor @Observable` ViewModel through `@State private var viewModel = BookingViewModel()`.
- Pass an observable ViewModel to an editing child with `@Bindable`; pass it read-only with `let`.
- A static placeholder may remain View-only. Add a Model only for real domain data.
- Keep Models as `let`-only value types with stable business IDs and displayable domain data. Add `Identifiable`, `Hashable`, or `Equatable` only where a call site needs it.
- Keep UI state, localization cases, accessibility IDs, and asset routing in the View/ViewModel layer. A typed enum may represent an icon choice; the View switches it to an `Image`.
- Add service/repository layers only for external fetch, save, or transformation work.

Represent screenshots of the same destination with ViewModel state and conditional UI in one View. For example, `isFilterPresented`, `selectedSegment`, and `loadState` live in the canonical ViewModel; small methods update them; the View renders `.sheet`, `.alert`, `.confirmationDialog`, `.popover`, or an overlay. Keep separate routes only for separate destinations.

## Components and preserved design names

- Do not create `Features/{Feature}/Components/` directories.
- Keep screen UI inline unless it is a component in `generated-component-groups.md`.
- Ignore file length, repetition, and visual similarity when deciding component boundaries.
- Put every canonical generated component in `UIComponents/{PascalCaseComponentName}/{Name}View.swift`, for example `UIComponents/DatePicker/DatePickerView.swift`. Component folder names use PascalCase.
- In empty-copy mode, files already staged together under `UIComponents/{PascalCaseComponentName}/` are generated siblings, not existing target matches. Consolidate every sibling into the single group canonical and preserve an explicit typed case/caller mapping for each raw member.
- Create one canonical component for every row in `generated-component-groups.md`, including one-caller rows. Use its planned `View`-suffixed name and rewrite every caller.
- Preserve an existing canonical component's behavior, API, and callers. Generalize it only for cases recorded in its generated group.
- Put shared navigation chrome in the common component layout, for example `UIComponents/BottomNavigation/BottomNavigationView.swift` and `UIComponents/AppTopBar/AppTopBarView.swift`.
- Prefer typed values and `@ViewBuilder` slots. Pass `Image` or a typed enum instead of an asset-name `String`.
- Expose canonical components and their configuration types as public APIs; keep supporting views private.
- Treat input affordances as editable values unless their recorded interaction contract is read-only. Use `Binding` for editable values, typed configuration for caller-selectable related states, and closures for caller-owned actions. Group related visibility controls into typed cases that render their selected region. Apply each declared prop/state in rendering or interaction and keep outer positioning in the caller.

Preserve design-authored identifiers exactly:

```swift
// Figma variable
static let bgPrim = ...

// Component state
@State private var selectedDate7 = ...
```

Keep both the marker and identifier through moves and canonicalization. Use semantic names only for new, unmarked tokens and types.

## Localization and constants

Conform to the target's existing localization system when it has one. For a greenfield project, use one `NSLocalizedString`-backed enum:

```swift
enum Localization: String {
    case welcome

    var localized: String {
        NSLocalizedString(rawValue, comment: "")
    }
}
```

- Render UI text with `Text(Localization.welcome.localized)`.
- Add every referenced raw value to `Localizable.xcstrings` or `Localizable.strings` with the exact display text from the design.
- Use `localized(_ args:)` plus `%@`/`%lld` catalog values for runtime substitutions.
- Render user/domain data with `Text(verbatim:)`.
- Pass resolved localized strings to `accessibilityCommon`.
- Put non-localized product constants—prices, versions, URLs, percentages, sample dates—in `AppConstants`.

## Design system and assets

- Route view dimensions through `DesignTokens`, colors through `Color(ColorNames.x)`, and images through `Image(IconNames.x)`.
- Keep marked Figma-variable tokens even when currently unused. Give new unmarked tokens semantic names and remove unused duplicates.
- Store colors in the top-level `Colors.xcassets`; keep its root `Contents.json` and one colorset per `ColorNames` entry.
- Preserve incoming custom assets. Use SF Symbols only where the input design uses them.
- Keep custom component image APIs typed (`Image` or enum), including leading/trailing icons.
- Define every referenced custom font in `AppFonts` and use `.custom(name, size: token, relativeTo: textStyle)` so Dynamic Type scales.
- When `.ttf` or `.otf` files exist, run the bundled script from the source root:

```bash
ruby <skill-dir>/references/register-fonts.rb .
```

- Preserve incoming modifier order while tokenizing or moving a generated Figma component; SwiftUI modifier order affects rendering.
- Use stack `spacing`, flexible `Spacer()`, or `Spacer(minLength:)` for gaps. Use `ScrollView` where Dynamic Type can grow the screen.
- Preserve HTML geometry except for changes required by the shared **Design-optimisation exception set** in `enhance-execute`. That set is exhaustive; do not infer additional responsive-layout exceptions.
- Flatten single-child and same-axis stacks when the child does not need a distinct layout or modifier boundary.
- Use `.clipShape(RoundedRectangle(...))` for rounded clipping.

### Safe areas

- Constrain screen-level content to the top safe area only so headers and controls clear the status bar, notch, and Dynamic Island. Do not apply the bottom safe-area inset or padding to the entire screen root. Let the root content extend to the bottom edge with `.ignoresSafeArea(.container, edges: .bottom)` when needed; never ignore the top safe area on a container that lays out screen content.
- Apply `.ignoresSafeArea(...)` to separate visual layers that must render edge to edge, such as the screen background, a dim/scrim overlay, or a modal sheet surface. A screen-content root may ignore only `.bottom` for the top-only safe-area contract; it must not ignore `.top` or `.all`.
- Treat custom popups, popovers, and bottom sheets as full-display overlays when the design places them relative to the screen edge. The scrim must cover the entire display, and a bottom sheet's background must extend through the bottom safe area to the screen edge. Preserve the design's visible sheet top position and height in full-display coordinates; do not apply a safe-area inset to the popup or sheet container because that shifts or resizes its geometry. Keep the surface edge to edge and add the runtime bottom safe-area inset only inside the footer or other bottom control region that needs protection. System-provided `.sheet` and `.popover` presentations may keep their native safe-area behavior.
- Never simulate a safe-area inset with fixed top or bottom padding, and never change a design spacing token merely to clear a notch, Dynamic Island, status bar, or home indicator on the selected simulator.
- Treat screenshot clearance as supporting evidence, not proof of correct implementation. Before recording `SAFE_AREA:PASS`, inspect the view hierarchy and modifiers: screen content must respect the top safe area without a root-level bottom inset; edge-to-edge visual layers may ignore safe areas; and any bottom safe-area inset must protect only the local controls that need it rather than shift or resize their entire container.

## Accessibility

Create `AccessibilityIdentifiers.swift` and one `DesignSystem/AccessibilityCommon.swift`. Its public API includes:

```swift
func accessibilityCommon(
    identifier: AccessibilityIdentifiers,
    suffix: String? = nil,
    label: String? = nil,
    hint: String? = nil,
    value: String? = nil,
    traits: AccessibilityTraitConfiguration = .init(),
    accessibilityElement: AccessibilityCommon.AccessibilityElement? = nil
) -> some View
```

Name the modifier type `AccessibilityCommon`. Centralize raw accessibility modifiers inside this utility; callers use the wrapper with localized label/hint values.

- Give interactive views button/selected/header traits as appropriate.
- Combine composite cards and rows for VoiceOver.
- Hide decorative images from accessibility.
- Give icon-only controls a tokenized 44×44 minimum target.
- Let text containers grow with Dynamic Type instead of pinning their width and height.

## Navigation and previews

When the design has tabs, create one `RootTabView` that owns `selectedTab`, renders the current destination, and hosts `UIComponents/BottomNavigation/BottomNavigationView`. Individual Screens render content only. Use the exact tab assets, labels, and colors recorded in `screenshot-mapping.md`. Register pushed destinations in the target's existing `NavigationStack` or router.

Every screen file ends with `#Preview { ... }` or a matching `PreviewProvider`.
For every canonical `Name.swift`, keep its typed light-theme color mappings and `#Preview` coverage in that component file. Render its distinct generated Figma configurations with existing design-system colors, no-op actions, or preview-local display state; add focused component tests when the target already has a component-test convention.

## Verification

From the inner Swift source root—the directory containing `Features/` and `DesignSystem/`—run the bundled probe unchanged:

```bash
bash <skill-dir>/references/acceptance-probes.sh
```

Batch all reported fixes, then rerun. Every `FAIL:` blocks completion; keep `WARN:` lines visible. Completion requires exit 0 and the script's literal `PROBES_RESULT:ALL_PASS warnings=N`.

When build verification is enabled, use the runnable app emitted by `enhance-execute` Step 7:

1. Load `swift-dev` and launch with its bundled `launch-simulator.sh`. Use the selected iPhone simulator with its status bar and camera cutout (notch or Dynamic Island) visible.
2. Read every reference screenshot at the exact generated-folder path from the kickoff prompt, then capture one uncropped, unmasked full-display simulator screenshot for every design state with `capture-screenshot.sh`. Do not search for alternate copies, and do not hide or normalize hardware-specific system regions.
3. Before comparing screenshots, inspect each screen's safe-area structure against the **Safe areas** rules above. A screen-content root that ignores `.top` or `.all`, or that applies the bottom inset to the entire root, fails even when the selected screenshot has no visible overlap; ignoring only `.bottom` is permitted. A custom popup or bottom sheet also fails when the safe-area inset shifts or resizes the whole overlay instead of padding only the controls that need protection. Fix the structure, rebuild, and recapture.
4. Compare each design/capture pair and inspect the status-bar and camera-cutout regions. Any text or interactive control under, behind, or obscured by either region is a visual failure. Fix it and recapture; never waive an obstruction as a simulator or hardware difference.
5. Write `.locofy/agent/memory/visual-verification.md`. Record the selected simulator once as `DEVICE:<model>`. For every screen, record `STATUS_BAR:VISIBLE CAMERA_CUTOUT:VISIBLE SAFE_AREA:PASS` only after both the structural inspection and the visible-overlap inspection pass; record `SAFE_AREA:FAIL` when either inspection fails.
6. Run:

```bash
bash <skill-dir>/references/visual-verify-probe.sh
```

The probe is a hard safe-area acceptance gate: missing per-screen evidence, hidden or cropped system UI, and every `SAFE_AREA:FAIL` block completion. Completion requires `VISUAL_RESULT:ALL_PASS`; then shut down the simulator started by the workflow. If the real build is blocked, report the build cause and do not claim a visual match. When `skipBuild` is set, skip build-dependent visual work.
